Parallax to confirm target regions (EU, US-West, APAC) and data residency constraints by 2026-04-29
Schedule pilot kickoff meeting for 2026-05-03, Maya to propose 2 slots

transcript_header: Date: 2026-04-22T15:00Z | Duration: 54 mins | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonas Reed (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Parallax VP Eng), Rahul Mehta (Parallax Platform), Sofia Green (Parallax Procurement)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, then we'll dive into the renewal and the edge expansion plan. Uh, we have about 50 minutes.
[00:12] Lena: Hi, Lena here. Thanks.
[00:15] Rahul: Rahul on the line.
[00:17] Sofia: Sofia here.
[00:20] Jonas: Jonas from Redwood, hello.
[00:23] Maya: Great, cool. Quick agenda — status on current usage and forecasts, target regions (you've mentioned EU and APAC), pricing options for committed capacity vs burst, and security/compliance checklist for private/VPC. Then next steps and pilot schedule. Any other items?
[00:40] Lena: No, that's it. Main thing for us is predictability — the product team needs headroom for the next 12 months.
[00:46] Rahul: Yep, and we have another constraint: some workflows must remain in EU for data residency, plus a small on-prem box for latency sensitive inference near factory sites.
[00:56] Maya: Got it. That maps to Redwood Dedicated + Private mix. Maybe Jonas can run through how we partition reserved pools and the private on-prem option.
[01:05] Jonas: Sure. So, for dedicated we provision GPU pools that are isolated — you get predictable throughput. For EU-only workloads we can either create an EU-dedicated pool or deploy Private (VPC) in your AWS account. For the on-prem low-latency sites we'd look at our Private on-prem package — lightweight runtime, limited model set; it's more of a co-managed install. Note there's work on certs, network, and KMS integration.
[01:32] Lena: When you say "co-managed" what kind of ops load are we talking about? We don't want to staff up to maintain clusters.
[01:39] Jonas: Good question. Co-managed means Redwood handles runtime updates and health monitoring, but network and physical access are with Parallax. Patching is automated; you'll need a single infra person to handle the appliance and VPN. We can add an ops runbook.
[01:50] Rahul: How about autoscaling? At edge sites we can't burst to the cloud.
[01:54] Jonas: Right — edge nodes are fixed capacity. For cloud-based Dedicated pools we have autoscale with warm standby nodes. We can route traffic with smart policies — latency-first for your factory inference, cost-first for batch processing.
[02:07] Maya: Quick pause — Sofia, from procurement perspective any constraints on multi-year terms or PO process?
[02:13] Sofia: We prefer annual commitments, but if pricing delta is big we can look at a 24-month. Also need vendor SOC2 Type II and clauses around data leakage.
[02:22] Maya: We have SOC2 and can provide ISO docs; we'll attach security pack.
[02:26] Jonas: Also note our audit logs and SSO (SAML) support — RBAC for team separation.
[02:31] Lena: Good. On capacity numbers — Rahul, can you go through current qps and token sizes?
[02:35] Rahul: Sure. Our primary endpoint is a reranking + short-completion flow. Peak is about 1,300 qps across US/EU, median sequence length is around 200 tokens, peaks at 600 tokens for some sessions. We do embeddings for search too, ~25k calls per day but low token count.
[02:56] Jonas: Helpful. For sizing, a mix of GTX-class and A100-like provisioning is common; we can recommend quantized models for the long sequences to save cost. Also intelligent KV cache and prefix caching will reduce token load for rerank flows.
[03:10] Lena: Is KV cache shared across regions or per pool? We need to ensure EU data never leaves region.
[03:15] Jonas: KV cache is per model instance/pool by default; for cross-region we can configure replication but for your case we'd keep EU cache in EU-only pools. The transcription here might show K V cache weirdly in the notes.
[03:28] Rahul: What's the expected latency hit with quantization? We tried a 4-bit model recently and saw a small uptick in tail latency.
[03:34] Jonas: There's a tradeoff — quantization gives lower cost and higher throughput, but depending on kernel selection and compilers you can see 5–20% latency variance. Our Optimize team tunes kernels per workload. We can run a benchmark using your prompt set.
[03:47] Maya: That's a good experiment. We'll propose a pilot: 4-week pilot, run benchmarks on your prod-ish dataset, compare hosted vs dedicated vs on-prem latencies, and then make a renewal commitment based on results.
[04:00] Lena: Timeline check — we need the renewal by end of May to sync with budget. A 4-week pilot starting early May works.
[04:06] Maya: Perfect. Pilot kickoff target — May 3rd. Jonas, you'll lead the technical onboarding?
[04:11] Jonas: Yes, I'll own the benchmark harness and test prompts. I'll need Rahul to supply sample traces and anonymized prompts.
[04:18] Rahul: I can export those; will scrub PII.
[04:21] Maya: Great. Pricing — quick structure. We can do: 1) Hosted pay-as-you-go with committed credit buffer; 2) Dedicated reserved pool with monthly commit and a discount ladder; 3) Private on-prem seat license + support fee. We usually show three scenarios with cost per effective token.
[04:39] Sofia: For procurement, we need to see the actual dollar differences and liability clauses. Also interested in committed burst capacity — sometimes we need headroom for launches.
[04:49] Maya: We'll include burst windows in the dedicated plan — a reserved baseline plus burst pooling with a defined burn rate. We'll enumerate RTO and credits.
[04:58] Lena: On the subject of region expansion — APAC is new for us. Which regions do you already support from Redwood's side?
[05:04] Jonas: We have hosted regions in US-East, US-West, EU-West, and APAC via partner edge regions. For Private we can deploy to any region your cloud account supports, but there is a provisioning lead time and compliance checklist.
[05:18] Rahul: How long for on-prem deployment? We have a pilot edge node we could test with.
[05:23] Jonas: Typically 2–4 weeks for an on-prem package: networking, cert exchange, KMS integration, and a POC model load. If you want the private control plane in your VPC, add another week.
[05:34] Maya: We should note any procurement approvals that might add delay. Sofia?
[05:37] Sofia: We'll need legal to review the master services agreement; timelines vary but typically two weeks if standard.
[05:44] Maya: Great. Any red flags or blockers from your side?
[05:48] Lena: Two things: 1) We must keep EU data residency for a subset of workloads; 2) We need a SLA for single-digit tail latency for the factory edge flows.
[05:56] Jonas: For SLA we can offer latency SLOs on dedicated pools and private installs. We'll scope acceptable tail lat numbers and put escalation procedures in the runbook.
[06:06] Rahul: Can we get synthetic traffic load tests against dedicated pools?
[06:09] Jonas: Yes — we'll provide a load test harness. I'll share a script and the expected metrics (p99, p95, cpu/gpu utilization).
[06:18] Maya: Okay, going back to pricing nuance — if you commit to 12 months of reserved capacity we can lock a better rate and include pilot credits to run benchmarks. If 24 months is possible, we can do deeper discounts but procurement approval is usually the bottleneck.
[06:33] Sofia: We'll evaluate both. Also need to see contract terms around termination and data deletion.
[06:39] Maya: We'll include standard data retention and deletion clauses; we support API-level data deletion and can provide attestations.
[06:46] Lena: On telemetry — we want token-level cost and latency breakdown. Is that available in the console?
[06:52] Jonas: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route, per-model token cost breakdowns, tracing hooks and simple evals to monitor quality regressions. We'll demo a console view in the pilot.
[07:02] Rahul: Regarding model versioning — if we pin a model for production, can you run a canary?
[07:06] Jonas: We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a cheaper variant if the canary regresses. You can set rollouts by percentage and time windows.
[07:14] Lena: For the on-prem low-latency nodes, we need strict encryption at rest and KMS.
[07:20] Jonas: We support customer-managed KMS/HSM for private installs. For hosted we encrypt at rest with our managed keys unless you bring your own.
[07:28] Sofia: Any dependencies for the private control plane to live in our VPC? We're particular about peering and egress.
[07:33] Jonas: We'll need a VPC peering or private link; requirements doc will list subnets, firewall rules, and NAT gateways. We'll provide a checklist.
[07:42] Maya: All right. Let's record decisions so far — pilot kickoff May 3rd, Redwood to provide pricing by Apr 26, Jonas to share benchmark harness by Apr 24, Parallax to share traces by Apr 25, procurement to review docs by Apr 28.
[07:59] Maya: Any other questions?
[08:02] Rahul: Slight thing — are there any constraints on model quantization affecting our evaluation metrics? We need to ensure quality drop is within tolerances.
[08:09] Jonas: We'll measure quality with your eval set and guardrails. We'll recommend quantization levels and present per-metric deltas.
[08:16] Lena: Also how do we handle emergency capacity for product launches? We need an MOP that explains runway and how to request spot capacity.
[08:23] Maya: We can include a runway plan and a defined rapid-provision process for launches; there are cost implications but doable.
[08:30] Sofia: For contract negotiation, does Redwood accept our standard indemnity language, or is there pushback?
[08:36] Maya: We can take a look; in our experience most enterprise legal teams iterate but it's workable. We'll flag any uncommon clauses.
[08:44] Jonas: One more technical note — for embedding storage we can recommend vector DB options and caching to reduce calls; that will influence cost.
[08:52] Rahul: Good point. We'll need guidance on best practices for embed caching.
[08:56] Jonas: I'll attach a short doc showing caching patterns and recommended TTLs.
[09:02] Maya: Okay, moving to wrap — I'll send the pricing scenarios and an annotated SOW that includes pilot scope. Jonas will attach the bench harness and ops runbook. Parallax will provide traces and procurement details.
[09:13] Lena: Sounds good.
[09:15] Sofia: Thanks, everyone.
[09:17] Maya: Great, thanks all. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the May 3rd kickoff and the documents.
[09:24] [END]
